correctness.rationale: Theorem 1.7 of arXiv:2604.02092 excludes every fixed finite number of RT^2_2 applications for BRT^3_{2,4}. A valid BRT^2_2 instance is uniformly an RT^2_2 instance whose infinite homogeneous solutions must be color 0, because the instance promise forbids even a finite color-1 homogeneous set of the supplied bound. Replacing each hypothetical bounded-pairs call by this one-call simulation contradicts Theorem 1.7.

value.rationale: The bounded Ramsey hierarchy is a central object of the source, and the pairs/triples transition is its first computability-theoretically nontrivial arity jump. Showing that no bounded finite iteration of the lower-arity bounded principle reaches BRT^3_{2,4} isolates that jump internally to the hierarchy, rather than only relative to the stronger ambient RT^2_2 benchmark.
